anomalies.observed: The BC817 NPN transistor Q2 has its base pin Q2.1 connected to the VCC net, while its emitter pin Q2.2 is connected to GND. R2 is connected between PWM and VCC, so it is not in series with Q2's base; Q2's base is tied directly to VCC.
anomalies.expected: For Q2 to act as the low-side driver for the P-MOS gate Q1.1, Q2.1 should be driven from the PWM signal through a current-limiting resistor, e.g. R2 between PWM and Q2.1, with Q2.2 at GND. An NPN base should not be tied directly to VCC when its emitter is grounded.
anomalies.impact: This creates a forward-biased base-emitter short from VCC to GND, causing excessive current and likely damage. Q2 will be permanently on, pulling Q1's gate low and enabling the fan supply regardless of PWM, removing the intended high-side PWM control.

parsed.summary: The design files contain a clear connectivity anomaly: Q2's base is tied directly to VCC while its emitter is grounded, instead of being driven from PWM through a resistor, creating a supply-to-ground short and forcing the fan power switch on.
